Standard: The air vehicle's short-term response to yaw control inputs in hover and low airspeed (up to 45 KGS) is no worse than Level 2 flying qualities as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Short-term Response to Yaw Control Inputs (Bandwidth) paragraph, unless pilot evaluation determines the air vehicle handling qualities are no worse than Level 2. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis to assess the yaw axis bandwidth and phase delay parameters as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Short-term Response to Yaw Control Inputs (Bandwidth) paragraph for each air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess the yaw axis bandwidth and phase delay parameters as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Short-term Response to Yaw Control Inputs (Bandwidth) paragraph for each air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess the yaw axis bandwidth and phase delay parameters as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Short-term Response to Yaw Control Inputs (Bandwidth) paragraph for selected combinations of air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE.
